text:
Bitcoin stabilized above $61,200 on June 30, staging a modest recovery as the brutal month-long capital flight from U.S. spot ETFs finally showed signs of exhaustion. After bleeding over $4 billion in June, spot inflows registered a positive net turn of $73 million, led by Fidelity's FBTC. However, broader market sentiment remains highly defensive. The immediate focus is centered on the July 1 execution of the EU's landmark MiCA regulations, which are already fracturing liquidity as exchanges delist non-compliant stablecoins, alongside the looming threat of Mt. Gox’s $9 billion bankruptcy distributions scheduled to begin this week.

In traditional finance, U.S. equities closed mixed as investors rotated into defensive consumer staples ahead of the second half of the year. The S&P 500 hovered at 7,410 while the 10-year Treasury yield held steady at 4.39%. This relative stability in yields has eased the short-term pressure on digital assets.
